h: Deer Parks, Diwali Lights and Steam Trains
p: Leicester has a wealth of follow-ups once the bouncing's over. Bradgate Park, just north-west of the city, is a wild, rugged landscape with roaming deer, rocky outcrops and the ruins of Bradgate House, the childhood home of Lady Jane Grey. It's a cracking place for a walk, with views across Leicestershire from Old John, the folly on the hill.
Closer to the centre, Abbey Park is a big, beautiful green space with the ruins of Leicester Abbey, gardens and play areas. It's ideal for a picnic and a run-around.

Leicester's Golden Mile on Belgrave Road is famous for its Indian restaurants, sweet shops and sari stores, and in autumn the city's Diwali celebrations light the whole road up in spectacular style. It's a brilliant place to grab a bite after a session.
Steam fans should head to Loughborough for the Great Central Railway, a heritage line where steam trains run on a double-track main line.

As for the jumping, the drill is simple: waiver done online before you set off, a bottle of water in the bag and clothes you can stretch in. An hour or so on the trampolines is usually plenty to leave most kids happily puffed out.
Toddler-focused sessions can be a gentler start for younger children, and older kids might enjoy the more active features, so check what this branch has on before booking.
Leicester Cathedral, where King Richard III was reburied in 2015, is also worth a visit.
